# Processor and transfer catalogue data

<!-- Generated by node ci/rule-packs/build-detection.mjs --write. -->

Exact-token catalogue rules identify payment integrations, AWS SDK use, S3 infrastructure resource types and two explicit AWS region settings. Every finding is a note asking the organisation to confirm processor safeguards and any transfer basis. No personal-data values are required by these cases.

Version: `2026.11.0`. Source: `rule-packs/processors.pack.json`.

The citation register records owner approval in principle; legal review remains pending. A finding requests review and does not establish a legal breach.

| Rule | Severity | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| `transfer.processor.paystack` | note | Confirm processor safeguards and any cross-border transfer basis. Sections 29 and 41-43; Articles 34 and 45; Schedule 5. |
| `transfer.processor.flutterwave` | note | Confirm processor safeguards and any cross-border transfer basis. Sections 29 and 41-43; Articles 34 and 45; Schedule 5. |
| `transfer.processor.aws` | note | Confirm processor safeguards and any cross-border transfer basis. Sections 29 and 41-43; Articles 34 and 45; Schedule 5. |
| `transfer.processor.aws.bucket` | note | Confirm processor safeguards and any cross-border transfer basis. Sections 29 and 41-43; Articles 34 and 45; Schedule 5. |
| `transfer.processor.aws.ireland` | note | Confirm processor safeguards and any cross-border transfer basis. Sections 29 and 41-43; Articles 34 and 45; Schedule 5. |
| `transfer.processor.aws.capetown` | note | Confirm processor safeguards and any cross-border transfer basis. Sections 29 and 41-43; Articles 34 and 45; Schedule 5. |

## Limits

Tokens indicate a reference, not actual network activity, processing, recipient role or a transfer. SDKs can be unused; region strings can occur in unrelated text. Matching is exact and case-sensitive, and does not resolve aliases or recognise arbitrary S3 virtual-hosted bucket names. Lock files stay excluded. SDK use alone cannot establish a processing region, so its metadata is deployment-dependent. The first catalogue is deliberately bounded to the sourced entries below. Processor metadata is retained in loaded rules and this reference; the existing v1 results contract reports the rule identifier and approved citation only. User-facing metadata output remains separate work under #64.

## Remediation and exceptions

Review the referenced integration and applicable contracts, record the actual data categories and processing regions, and confirm safeguards and any applicable transfer basis. Use the existing justified-exception configuration when a deliberately retained reference does not need further action.

## Processor metadata

| Rule | Data categories | Usual region |
|---|---|---|
| `transfer.processor.paystack` | customer contact details; payment and transaction details | Deployment-dependent; confirm the contracted processing and storage regions. |
| `transfer.processor.flutterwave` | customer contact details; payment and transaction details | Deployment-dependent; confirm the contracted processing and storage regions. |
| `transfer.processor.aws` | application-defined stored data | Deployment-dependent; confirm the contracted processing and storage regions. |
| `transfer.processor.aws.bucket` | application-defined stored data | Deployment-dependent; confirm the contracted processing and storage regions. |
| `transfer.processor.aws.ireland` | application-defined data | Europe (Ireland); confirm that this configuration is used. |
| `transfer.processor.aws.capetown` | application-defined data | Africa (Cape Town); confirm that this configuration is used. |

## Verification

Run `dotnet test tests/Corpus.Tests -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~DetectionPackTests` for exact locations and measured synthetic precision/recall.

These are unsigned release-source packs. Tests sign only in memory with the labelled development key. Production signing, embedding and publication are separate release operations; no development signature is shipped.
